errors.current: atasharrafu always takes bi-: bi-an + a verb (bi-an ataqaddama). Without bi- the phrase sounds broken.
errors.problem: The card marks أَتَشَرَّفُ أَنْ أَتَقَدَّمَ as wrong and says that without bi- the phrase 'sounds broken'. Dropping a preposition before أَنْ / أَنَّ is regular in Arabic (حذف حرف الجر قبل أن وأنّ قياسي), and أتشرف أن أتقدم is common in real formal letters. bi-an is the preferred formal choice, but the other form is not an error. Karim says the same in dialogue.lines[8] ('نَسْتَعْمِلُ دَائِمًا «بِأَنْ»').
errors.fix: atasharrafu takes bi-: bi-an + a verb (bi-an ataqaddama). You will also see atasharrafu an…, but bi-an is the classic formal choice.
errors.alsoChange: dialogue.lines[8]: soften دَائِمًا (e.g. وَبَعْدَهَا نَسْتَعْمِلُ عَادَةً «بِأَنْ») and adjust the English 'always'

errors.problem: In أَهْلًا يَا مُدِير! the word is a vocative, not the first part of an iḍāfa. '(of)' is misleading.

errors.problem: الْوَاحِدَة means 'one' (السَّاعَةُ الْوَاحِدَةُ = one o'clock). 'The first' is الْأُولَى. The auto glossary has the same gloss for this exact form.

notes.note: أُعْلِنَ النَّتَائِجُ is marked wrong ('plurals of things take the feminine'). A verb before a broken plural may be masculine or feminine in classical grammar, so the feminine is the preferred norm, not the only correct form. Consider 'usually take'.
'istamaʿa always needs ilā': it also takes li- (اِسْتَمَعَ لَهُ). 'needs a preposition, usually ilā' would be safer.
'It's the second-to-last week of the course' contradicts day 85 ('the last week of the course'). Day 88 is in week 13, the final week.
Past verbs are glossed as 'pronounces (past)', 'expresses (past)', 'tries (past)', 'apologises (past)'. '(he) pronounced', '(he) expressed' etc. would be clearer.
«يَعْنِي» وَ«كَيْفَ أَقُولُ» تُعْطِيكَ: with two coordinated items the dual تُعْطِيَانِكَ is more careful. The feminine singular is tolerable.
إِلَيْكُمْ نَشْرَةَ الْأَخْبَار is defensible (ilaykum as a verbal noun, 'take'), but broadcasters mostly say إِلَيْكُمْ نَشْرَةُ الْأَخْبَار.
Names are lowercased in the transliteration in the same line where others are capitalised: 'ṣalāḥi d-dīn', 'muḥammad ʿAlī', 'landan'.
رُخَام vs مَرْمَر: in most of the Arab world both mean 'marble'. 'Alabaster' for مَرْمَر is right for the Egyptian name of the mosque, but a culture note could say so.

summary: Read the whole days-81-90 export (days 81-90: Arabic lines, segs, taps, mistake cards, quizzes, readings) against MSA grammar, and spot-checked the auto glossaries for the forms involved. Found 19 errors (3 major, 16 minor). Arabic and grammar: one wrong case (أَيَّ for nominative أَيُّ in an embedded question, day 88), one elative agreement slip (الْمُشْكِلَةَ الْأَكْبَرَ, day 86), and one over-strict rule in the day-82 formal-letter mistake card (أتشرف أن is not 'broken'). Everything else in the passive, conditionals, inna/anna, kāna, numbers, ordinals and the formal-letter formulas is correct. Most findings are tap glosses carried over from another sentence or another sense: عَشَرَ glossed 'twelfth' on 18th/19th, the second نَاحِيَةٍ glossed 'on the one hand' (also on the quiz answer for 'on the other hand'), مِنْ glossed with the 'please' sense in the min/mina lesson, عُنْوَان glossed 'address' on headline day, تُكَرِّرَ glossed '(she) repeats' in 'please repeat (you)', and اِكْتَشَفَ glossed 'was discovered' (also in the auto glossary). One engine problem: an English letter name followed by the bare letter gives a doubled name in the transliteration. Tap glosses checked: 1224 (in 383 tap lines); wrong: 34, across 15 findings. Round-1 fixes in this chunk (days 81-90 cards, -īna/-ayni rules, al-yawmu, hamzat waṣl spellings) look correct, and I found no new problems introduced by them.
